data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word "ashaara", meaning 'ten'. This name holds a significant place in Islamic history, as it is the number of heavenly angels sent to each prophet to record their deeds. The name Ashras carries the meaning “Ten” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashras usually hope their child will grow to embody ten and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashras total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic tradition, the term "Ashras" is used to refer to a group of ten things. This includes the ten Apostles or companions of Prophet Muhammad SAW, the ten verses of Surah Al-Maut (the chapter on Death), ten traits of a believer, and so on. It emphasizes the importance of unity and completeness within groups or concepts.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the concept of Ashras holds deep significance. The Islamic belief asserts that every prophet is sent ten angels to record their deeds. This highlights the importance of leading a virtuous life, as every action will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment. Moreover, the term Ashras also appears in a number of Hadiths and Prophetic sayings, further emphasizing its importance in Islamic teachings.
